title: Agent Manifest
description: A declarative agent manifest that projects into an executable agent. The manifest carries a base 'template' agent definition plus a list of resources (tools and models) that are resolved at runtime. Tool resources enable machine-specific and user-specific tool configurations, such as MCP servers, to be referenced by name and resolved against the current execution context.

name.description: Unique identifier for the manifest. Used in manifest selection and resolution.

displayName.description: Human-readable name of the manifest, displayed in UI.

description.description: Description of the agent's capabilities and purpose. Shown in selection UI.

metadata.description: Additional metadata including authors, tags, version, and other arbitrary properties.

template.description: The base agent definition that this manifest projects into. Tool resources listed in 'resources' are resolved and appended to the template's tools when the agent is created.

parameters.description: Parameter schema for configuring the agent's behavior. Parameters may be referenced within the manifest using {{paramName}} notation.

resources.description: Resources required by the agent, such as tools and models. Tool resources are resolved at runtime based on the execution context (user, machine, workspace).

toolResource.description: A reference to a tool that is resolved at runtime. 'id' selects the resolution strategy and 'name' identifies the specific resource.

kind.description: Resource kind discriminator. Always 'tool' for tool resources.

id.description: Tool resource type that selects how the tool is resolved. Common values: 'mcp-server-entity' (resolve an mcp-server entity by entity name, see 'name'), 'fixed' (resolve a built-in toolset by name). An unknown id fails session load with "Tool resource '<id>:<name>' could not be resolved".

name.description: Tool resource name. For 'fixed' type, this is the built-in toolset name (e.g., 'workspace-entity', 'filesystem'). For 'mcp-server-entity' type, this value is appended to each MCP-server search prefix, in priority order, to form a candidate entity name; the first existing entity that has an 'mcp-server' property wins. Search prefixes, highest priority first: the machine profile 'computer-user-profiles/users/username/<user>/computers/hostname/<host>/copilot/mcp-servers', then '${USER}/mcp-servers', then 'defaults/mcp-servers'. The mcp-server entity must therefore be named with this value as its final name component under one of those prefixes (e.g. 'defaults/mcp-servers/github'). Resolution keys off the entity name, not the mcp-server 'serverName' field.

options.description: Tool-specific configuration options. The structure depends on the tool type.

modelResource.description: A reference to a model resource required by the agent.

kind.description: Resource kind discriminator. Always 'model' for model resources.

name.description: Optional human-readable name for the model resource.
